id: MATRESCENCE Development Showing-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda-Humanitix
name: MATRESCENCE Development Showing
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda
long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Photo by Charlie Jewell

name: The Velvet Glove Plays the Songs of The Velvet Underground
venue: 52 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The Velvet Glove returns following last January’s breakout show to revisit the heart of the Velvet Underground’s gritty urban realism, bridging the Velvet’s bright jangly chaos and Lou Reed’s lyric beauty.

 

The Glove reunites three musicians from early 70s Dunedin Band Cripple - bass player John Dodd (Midge Marsden, The Chaps, Skin and Bone), sax player Chris Nichol (The Dunstan Rangers, The Zimmermans) and Lindsay Gregory (The Dunstan Rangers, Heaven Bent Choir) on keyboards. They’re joined by drummer Sean Barker (Wooden Box Band, The Zimmermans) and guitarist Bill Nichol (Baby, Pegasus) for another walk on the wild side.

id: 'TONES OF SILENCE' - FUTUNA CHAPEL IN B&W - PUBLIC TALKS 2026-67 Futuna Close, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: 'TONES OF SILENCE' - FUTUNA CHAPEL IN B&W - PUBLIC TALKS 2026
venue: 67 Futuna Close, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - PUBLIC TALKS 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ exhibition explores through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will reveal the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

Step inside Futuna Chapel for three captivating Sunday afternoon talks covering black-and-white photography, heritage architecture, and Aotearoa New Zealand’s built history, from 2:00pm to 3:30pm during the Futuna Exhibition.

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend these events and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the WHF events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust. 

Please register to attend the public talks to ensure you get a seat. Seats are limited. There is no set ticket price. The gift of koha is prefered.

venue: 9 Batchelor Street, Newlands, Wellington 6037, New Zealand
long_description:
For the first time in 10 years - Mark Moroney & David Shanhun are reuniting for a series of intimate shows across New Zealand in 2026. This special tour brings their signature blend of world-class guitar playing, heartfelt songwriting, rich harmonies, and light-hearted banter back to audiences around the country. Expect an evening of unforgettable music, plenty of laughs, and the kind of connection that only comes from two great friends & musicians sharing the stage.

This is your chance to see these two acclaimed guitarists and singer-songwriters LIVE in your town!

NEWLANDS COMMUNITY CENTRE - SAT 5th DEC.

💫 Seated Show

💫 Intimate Setting

💫 Cheaper $15 tickets for under 18s

💫 Doors open 6:30pm / show starts at 7pm (8:45pm finish).

Don’t miss your chance to experience these two exquisite musicians, live and up close.

MARK MORONEY

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

"Once in a while you see an artist who is out of the ordinary." - The Shirley Ryder Show

David Shanhun has opened for Rock legends Foreigner, & Heart, and has performed in NZ, Japan, Australia, and the UK. His exquisite guitar work shines under his superb storytelling and songwriting. He's performed with Grammy Award winner Bryan White, and is known for his engaging live shows and heartfelt tunes.

name: Free Women's Self Defence Course
venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

name: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connections, Reflections and Possibilities
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Come and join Te Whiri Whītau as we celebrate a year of learning, making, connecting and dreaming together.

We warmly invite you to join in conversation, connection and celebration as we reflect on the year that has been and share our aspirations for the future. This gathering is an opportunity to learn more about the work of Te Whiri Whītau, hear about current and emerging research, meet our researchers and collaborators, and explore opportunities for collaboration, partnership, creative practice and research.

Over the course of the event, we'll share research highlights, introduce our new visual identity, and open conversations about the role that fibres, textiles and materials can play in creating thriving communities, cultures, environments and economies.

Whether you are a researcher, practitioner, student, industry partner, community organisation or supporter of our work, we would love you to join us as we strengthen connections, celebrate achievements, and look ahead to what's possible together.

Light refreshments will be served.

name: This Is Grief: On the Road - Wellington
venue: 57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Let’s talk about grief.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a series of free community conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O’Connor for an honest, informal conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the tidy timelines, clichés and expectations we’re often given.

There is no right kind of grief, and no right way to show up.

You might be grieving someone you love. You might be supporting someone who is. You might work alongside grief in your community or simply want us to get better at talking about something that touches all of us.

You are welcome to come and listen. You don’t have to share your story, speak, or have the right words.

Friday 13 November 2026
12.30pm–2pm
Unity Books, Wellington
Free event

Kirsten is the author of The Year After Kahlia, STAY and Tiny Invitations, and founder of This Is Grief.

Come as you are.

The collection of music entitled Rivering is written by saxophonist and vocalist Lily Rose Atu, and is deeply inspired by her love of jazz and neo-soul. This will be our last gig with the incredible pianist Paulina who will be heading overseas a few days after this show. Come and listen to the music we have created together for a final time!

Door sales: $15

id: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman-Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

https://www.naumihotels.com/naumi-studio-wellington
https://sojournhotels.co.nz/
https://www.themarionhostel.com/

name: INTIMATE EARTH | Film Adjacent Experimental Film Symposium
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Film Adjacent presents Intimate Earth, a symposium dedicated to the aesthetic, cultural and political energies of experimental film in Aotearoa and beyond. Intimate Earth celebrates ways of seeing in distinction to dominant modes of audio-visual media in the twenty-first century. The symposium will assemble artists, curators and audiences around micro and macrocosmic imaginations of a world otherwise. 

This will be a two-day event, featuring six programmes, multiple roundtable discussions, and a filmmaking workshop. Attendees can come and go as they please.

Saturday 21st November

9am - 12pm:  Attentive Medias: Filmmaking workshop with Tiso Ross and Tyler Shane Tesolin

1pm - Doors Open

2pm - 3:50pm:  Indigenous avant-garde. Pres. by Missy Molloy & Fernanda Miño + artist talk

4:30pm - 5:45pm: Aotearoa Poetry Film Festival 2026. Pres. by Alfio Leotta

6:30pm - 8:30pm: Electromorphic Poetry. Pres. by Tyler Shane Tesolin + video introduction by R. Bruce Elder


Sunday 22nd of November

1pm - Doors Open

2pm - 3:50pm: Film Ecologies; Toxic Legacies. Pres. by Christopher Thompson + Artist talk with Fiona Amundsen and Tim Corballis

4:20pm - 6:10pm: Student Programme: Unbound: Bodies, Whenua & Becoming. Pres. by Lucy Heath (Contrast Massey), followed by Student Films & Roundtable on student filmmaking.

6:45pm - 8:00pm: Cinema for Friends + music performance by The Last Dream

long_description:
NYMPHO welcomes Chippy Nonstop to Pōneke in collaboration with her own party series, PEP RALLY, for a cross-continental meeting on the dancefloor. One for the history books.

Chippy Nonstop is a versatile DJ, rapper, and producer whose high-energy sets seamlessly blend global club, rap, and bass-driven sounds. She thrives across contexts from queer-focused underground nights to fashion events and more commercial stages bringing her unique energy to every floor. Key shows include Berghain, Live From Earth, DGTL, Ultra, the Mugler Fashion Show and has shared lineups with VTSS, LSDXOXO, Honey Dijon and many more. Chippy also runs her own party series and upcoming label Pep Rally, centering FLINTA, BIPOC, and queer representation*.

LINEUP:

CHIPPY NONSTOP (CAN)

BABETECH

CURRENT BIAS

WELMIE

ODEIOUS

DOOM100001B2B75ARROWHEADS

MC MAN(K)ILA

NYMPHO is a dance-focused queer club night with visual and performance art styles woven into high energy DJ sets. We strive to create a safe, inclusive and transcendent club experience which celebrates gender euphoria, body positivity and sexual liberation. Our kaupapa of lifting up marginalised communities extends from our audience and lineups to our musical philosophies - with genre-diverse sets centred around QBIPOC rooted genres such as techno, house and emergent queer sounds. As well as spotlighting the best of Aotearoa’s diverse queer talent, NYMPHO has brought international icons to our long white cloud, including Isabella Lovestory, horsegiirL, Doss, TAAHLIAH, Ninajirachi, Umru, MGNA Crrrta, Kevin Aviance, MikeQ, Pxssy Palace, Jasmine Infiniti, Estoc, Clearcast and DJ G2G.

Ki ngā iwi Mana Whenua ō Te Whanganui-a-Tara, tēnei te tuku mihi ki ā koutou katoa. We acknowledge Te Āti Awa, Ngāti Mutunga, Ngāti Tama, Ngāti Ruanui, Taranaki Whānui, Ngāti Toa Rangatira as Mana Whenua of Wellington/Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

May the flames of your peoples never extinguish, but only to burn brighter. Thank you for your enduring presence! Mauri Ora!! 🖤🤍❤️

Concession tickets are available for low wage, unemployed or financially insecure nymphs. If you can't afford a ticket you can get in touch with us via Instagram. No nymphs left behind!

EPILEPSY WARNING: Strobe lighting and other intense lighting effects will be used during this show. It will not be safe for those with epilepsy and other conditions with sensitivity to light.

name: AoJO November Improvisation Workshops: Beginner
venue: Level 5/39 Webb Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

venue: 13 Vennell Street, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
$25

Limited door sales for $30

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

long_description:
We warmly invite you to this BWB Talk with Aroha Harris to celebrate the publication of her new book, We Are What We Write.

Aroha Harris (Te Rarawa, Ngāpuhi) MNZM is an award-winning historian and Associate Professor of History at Waipapa Taumata Rau–the University of Auckland. In this wide-ranging collection of essays, she brings together more than two decades of writing, drawing from public lectures, essays, tributes and previously unpublished reflections. Written with characteristic warmth and intellectual clarity, the collection explores the tensions between policy and people, the reshaping of Māori-Crown relationships, and the everyday acts of remembering that shape Māori worlds.

Please join us at the National Library | Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa for this event with Aroha Harris.

long_description:
Immerse yourself in a breathtaking 3-hour cinematic journey into the world’s most spectacular marine environments. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour brings together an extraordinary collection of short films celebrating the beauty, power and wonder of our oceans.

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. Meet the passionate divers, fearless surfers, dedicated ocean advocates, ocean explorers and marine scientists whose lives are shaped by their connection to the sea.

Featuring spectacular underwater cinematography, heart-stopping ocean adventures and intimate stories of the people who dedicate their lives to exploring and protecting our oceans, every film offers a fresh perspective on the world beneath the waves.

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.

The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power. Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

Find out more at https://oceanfilmfestivalworldtour.com/tickets-new-zealand/

 

The Ocean Film Festival is exempt from Classification, but all swearing has been beeped out.

Recommended age 10+

id: BWB Talk: Aroha Harris at the National Library-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: BWB Talk: Aroha Harris at the National Library
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We warmly invite you to this BWB Talk with Aroha Harris to celebrate the publication of her new book, We Are What We Write.

Aroha Harris (Te Rarawa, Ngāpuhi) MNZM is an award-winning historian and Associate Professor of History at Waipapa Taumata Rau–the University of Auckland. In this wide-ranging collection of essays, she brings together more than two decades of writing, drawing from public lectures, essays, tributes and previously unpublished reflections. Written with characteristic warmth and intellectual clarity, the collection explores the tensions between policy and people, the reshaping of Māori-Crown relationships, and the everyday acts of remembering that shape Māori worlds.

Please join us at the National Library | Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa for this event with Aroha Harris.

When: Thursday 19 November, 6pm (doors open 5.30pm)

Where: National Library Auditorium (best entrance via Aitken St)

Free event. No RSVP needed, but if you're planning to come we'd love to know – it helps us manage numbers. Please click RSVP to register your interest.

long_description:
🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

📅 Event details

Date: Saturday 28 November 2026

Time: 1:00–3:00 PM

Location: Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub

Address: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington

Cost: FREE

Spaces: Limited to 25 registrations

📱 What to bring

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

A free AI chatbot app, if you already have one

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

Don't have an AI app? No worries! You can follow the live demonstrations or work with a partner.

💛 Why we're doing this

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

🎟️ Reserve your FREE place today.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with venue support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

Please note: This is a practical learning workshop, not a formal IELTS assessment or band-scoring session.

name: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

id: Greccio the Song, a sacred musical inspired by the life of St Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio-15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Greccio the Song, a sacred musical inspired by the life of St Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio
venue: 15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026 at 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

Enquiries: vineyardhouse.nz@gmail.com

long_description:
Fungi for food security 🍄

Mushrooms are one of the fastest ways to grow nutritious food at home. In this hands-on workshop, Mihau and Valetta of Matariki Mushrooms show you simple, permaculture-inspired, low-tech methods for turning everyday waste like straw, sawdust and garden offcuts into high-quality, protein-rich food in just a few weeks.

What you'll learn

Native fungi of Aotearoa: an introduction to our native species, their traditional uses and their role in our ecosystems

Ways to grow: an overview of different growing methods, from low-tech to more advanced, and which suit growing at home

Hands-on: make your own grow kit with gourmet native oyster mushrooms

Expanding your own spawn: learn how to multiply your spawn, which makes growing mushrooms at home much more affordable, almost free

What you'll take home

Your own grow kit and spawn, ready for a first harvest in about 4 weeks

The know-how to keep producing mushrooms at home for years to come

When: Saturday 16 January 2027, 1–5pm

Where: Kaicycle Urban Farm, 5 Hospital Road, Newtown, Wellington (an outdoor farm setting, so dress for the weather)

Included: all materials, an introduction to fungi ecology and a hands-on practical session

Please bring: two clean 2L ice-cream containers with lids, and a plate to share for afternoon tea (shared kai)

Early bird: $90 until 20 December, then $100

Bookings essential: spaces are limited, please book online

Gift idea: a ticket makes a great Christmas present

Afterpay available: pay in 4 interest-free instalments

Keep growing: Advanced workshop

Ready for the next step? Join our Advanced · Logs & Liquid Culture workshop on Saturday 30 January: grow native shiitake on logs, make dowel spawn and liquid culture, and take home your own inoculated log and a syringe of pekepeke-kiore (a native cousin of lion's mane). Book both workshops and get a free copy of our book "Family of Forest and Fungi - He Tukutuku Toiora."

long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

name: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - PUBLIC TALKS 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ exhibition explores through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will reveal the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

Step inside Futuna Chapel for three captivating Sunday afternoon talks covering black-and-white photography, heritage architecture, and Aotearoa New Zealand’s built history, from 2:00pm to 3:30pm during the Futuna Exhibition.

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend these events and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the WHF events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust. 

Please register to attend the public talks to ensure you get a seat. Seats are limited. There is no set ticket price. The gift of koha is prefered.

long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

long_description:
VENUE UPDATED! SEE BELOW!

We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

NEW LOCATION: Wētā Workshop Cinema, 7 Weka Street (to the right of the trolls)

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

long_description:
S-ence returns to the Cuba St Tavern Courtyard with a special concept night to warm your winter blues.

Essential Selections feat
Matt Drake | Jen Kyle | Coda

After playing alongside each other at Arkadien last year, this powerhouse-trio hatched the idea of playing a concept night together where they each would go a bit more free-range and play sets and tracks that riff off each other. Not quite a B2B session but definitely as much fun.

So with that in mind - S-ence is proud to welcome Matt Drake back to the capital.

Matt Drake has been a champion of timeless electronic body music in Aotearoa for more than two decades. His style is a hypersonic melting pot of cosmic house jams and hypnotic Detroit techno grooves. Drawing inspiration from the astral arpeggios of 70s Krautrock, ragged Balearic vagabond synth pop of the 80s and proto-rave machine rhythms of the 90s.

Jen Kyle's cult following continues to grow - synonymous for her DJ sets where she journeys through everything from techno to disco, punk to funk, soul to hip hop, new wave and beyond.

Rounding out the triptych - DJ Coda can't wait to return to the CST and the opportunity to delve in and out of some different genre boxes. Hot off sets at CubaDupa and Baobab @ Newtown Festival, the courtyard is one of his favourite places to play.

Expect an Essential Selection spanned early and lates sets from all three selectors with lots of fun on and off the decks.

TICKETS ON SALE SATURDAY 18 APRIL.
LIMITED EARLYBIRDS & PRESALES

Make an evening of it and come for a late afternoon drink and repas (meal : ) and get into the groove when the beats start.
Early doors, early night.

Matt Drake (Auck)

long_description:
$25

Limited door sales for $30

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

long_description:
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

id: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Home Alone Music is proud to announce the Aotearoa and Australian tour in celebration of Timothy Blackman's new album 'Between the Islands' (HAM050) in January/February 2027.  

In Aotearoa, there will be full band shows in Wellington and Palmerston North. 

For the full band shows, Timothy's backing band will consist of Tessa Dillion on bass/backing vocals (Mystery Waitress and Tessa de Lyon) and Olivia Campion on drums (Mystery Waitress and Yumi Zouma).

Between the Islands was recorded with a live studio band consisting of Blackman, Tessa Dillon (Mystery Waitress), and Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (French for Rabbits, Dateline). Lee Prebble recorded and mixed their performances at The Surgery Recording Studio in Omāroro, Newtown, Wellington over three days in May 2025. Additional overdubs were performed and recorded by Blackman’s longtime collaborator Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) at her home in Wellington. The album was mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago, Illinois.  Album artwork by Alex Thornton.  


----

Timothy Blackman is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington based singer-songwriter, recording artist and founder of independent Aotearoa New Zealand record label Home Alone.

Since his first EP in 2006, Blackman has released a string of acclaimed records such as Modern Sprawl, I've Never Lived, Everyone Needs Something to Hold On To and Brightest Days. Blackman grew up in the Wellington region, began playing violin at five and guitar at ten, and was performing in bands around the Lower Hutt/Wellington area as a teenager. 

His music has since taken him from the bedrooms and small venues of Aotearoa to stages across Europe, the UK, United States and Australia, where he has performed alongside artists including The Mountain Goats and Scout Niblett. His music sits in an intimate space, flitting somewhere between the introspective songwriting of Bill Callahan and Bonnie Prince Billy, and the DIY spirit of New Zealand icon Chris Knox. His songs are personal and unvarnished: thoughtful, melancholic and often quietly funny, with a fascination for place, memory, displacement and the strange details of everyday life.

name: 'TONES OF SILENCE' - FUTUNA CHAPEL IN B&W - EXHIBITION 2026
venue: 67 Futuna Close, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - EXHIBITION 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ -explored through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will explore the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

"Generally, the older the equipment, the greater the personal input of the photographer is required and therefore the greater the commitment and individuality. Often, you can look at a 19th-century photograph and tell who the photographer is. You certainly can't do that today. It isn't only the camera and lens, but also the type of film (or in those days, glass plate), the developer used and how the print is made onto particular types of paper. Each gives a distinct interpretation".

John Grace - email - 18/06/25

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the exhibition events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.  Please register

REGISTRATION IS PREFERRED TO ATTEND THIS EVENT. Note that the sunday exhibition hours are 11:00am to 2:00pm. This allows for the public talks that commence at 2:00pm.

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. id: AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography-2/8 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography
venue: 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography

Expanding the frame to fit the evolving world of image making.

Commercial photography has always evolved alongside technology, creativity and client needs. Today, changes happen faster than ever, the lines between photography, video, motion, stop motion and content creation are increasingly blurred. Agencies and clients are after new ways to tell stories and the expectations and skills in image-making shifts with them.

But what does that actually mean for photographers?

Whether you've spent decades behind the camera, are just finding your feet, or you’re somewhere in between, change always brings questions, sometimes challenges and of course, plenty of opportunities.


So do we need to adapt? What skills are becoming more valuable? How are agencies approaching creative production? And how can we evolve our businesses and creative practice without losing sight of what makes our work distinctive?

On Tuesday 1 December, we’ll unpack these questions and more with our guest speakers: 

Ashley Alexander | Photographer, Videographer & Creative

Ashley will share his perspective from behind the camera, how his practice has evolved and the opportunities he's found working across different forms of image-making.

Josh Rollo | Senior Producer, VML

Josh brings the agency perspective, sharing insights into how creative production is changing, what clients are looking for and how agencies are navigating an ever-evolving landscape.

This isn't about having all the answers or trying to be everything to everyone. It's about understanding what's happening around us, learning from each other and recognising the opportunities.

Tuesday 1 December | 6pm

VML, 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mt Victoria, Wellington

Free for AIPA and NZIPP members | $10 for non-members.

Come along and bring your questions, share your experiences and meet other photographers in the industry. Whether you're established, emerging or just curious about what's next, there's a place for you in this conversation.

Good conversations. New perspectives. A chance to think about what's possible. And yes, there'll be pizza!

long_description:
RayWave and Glasshead collab to present a surprise night of live music for Sunday November 15th at Valhalla.

Indie-rock solo artist Jack Bromwich headlines the evening with his band. Having played numerous shows across the country, Bromwich’s sound has evolved with every release. Following the release of his debut EP Poser, Freak with critical acclaim from the student radio network and local music journalists, Bromwich’s voice has started to spread around the national music scene, taking the hearts of listeners.

Hexxer is the solo alt-rock project of Sam Butler. Originally from Ōtautahi (Christchurch), Butler has been developing Hexxer since 2024, releasing four singles and performing across the Ōtautahi music scene. Now based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), Hexxer has become part of the city's independent music community, with a lineup featuring Hayden Lam, Max Ware, and Moses Buda.

Blue Lady make their debut performance with a set showcasing what the new group has been exploring within their sound throughout the course of 2026. Blue Lady is the fresh, brand new side project of Tia Cranefield and Cara Bryant (Banjo Ben and The Breeze), Zac Irving and Ned Rainey (Grove) and James Cochrane (Raffla). Blue Lady test out their new alternative sound on the 15th.

The evening will be opened by an unannounced secret artist, revealed only days before the event.
