venue: 7 Weka Street, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
long_description:
VENUE UPDATED! SEE BELOW!

We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

NEW LOCATION: Wētā Workshop Cinema, 7 Weka Street (to the right of the trolls)

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
***UPDATE: FILM WILL START AT 7:30 SHARP***

WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

RayWave and Glasshead collab to present a surprise night of live music for Sunday November 15th at Valhalla.

Indie-rock solo artist Jack Bromwich headlines the evening with his band. Having played numerous shows across the country, Bromwich’s sound has evolved with every release. Blue Lady test out their new alternative sound on the 15th.

The evening will be opened by an unannounced secret artist, revealed only days before the event.

id: Double Feature: Leading Through Change and Uncertainty & Courageous Leadership in the VUCA World-33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Double Feature: Leading Through Change and Uncertainty & Courageous Leadership in the VUCA World
venue: 33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Note: This is an in-person only event at Rutherford House, Vic Uni, Bunny Street Wellington 6011

About this event:

Join the PMI New Zealand Wellington Branch on 18 November for an engaging double-feature session with Gina Barlow and Iain Fraser.

Gina will open the evening with an interactive discussion on how leaders can respond effectively to change and uncertainty. Her session will explore the difference between certainty and clarity, introduce four project terrains, share “radar” questions for detecting weak signals, outline an adaptive operating cadence, and unpack the CALM leadership routine as a practical approach for navigating complexity.

Iain Fraser will then build on these themes with insights on courageous leadership in a VUCA world — where volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity demand clear thinking, sound judgment, and confident action from project leaders.

This session is designed for project professionals, change leaders, and decision-makers who want practical ideas for leading well when the environment is shifting and the path ahead is not fully clear.

About the Presenter:

Gina Barlow is an experienced assurance and transformation professional with a passion for helping organisations and project teams navigate complexity, change and uncertainty. As Practice Lead for Assurance at Nonsuch, she works across complex projects and programmes, bringing together governance, risk, change management, assurance and practical delivery experience. Gina is particularly interested in what helps people and teams remain effective when the path ahead isn’t entirely clear.

Iain Fraser, PMP, PMI Fellow is an author, trainer, and internationally recognised project, program, and portfolio management leader. He is known for his work in governance, benefits realisation, value management, and organisational change, and previously served as Chair of PMI’s global Board of Directors.

Course Identifier: PMINZWTGN18112026

PDU Claim Code:0129YMU0Q2




This event is hosted by the PMINZ Wellington Branch

name: Greccio the Song, a sacred musical inspired by the life of St Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio
venue: 15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026 at 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

Enquiries: vineyardhouse.nz@gmail.com

S-ence returns to the Cuba St Tavern Courtyard with a special concept night to warm your winter blues.

Essential Selections feat
Matt Drake | Jen Kyle | Coda

After playing alongside each other at Arkadien last year, this powerhouse-trio hatched the idea of playing a concept night together where they each would go a bit more free-range and play sets and tracks that riff off each other. Not quite a B2B session but definitely as much fun.

So with that in mind - S-ence is proud to welcome Matt Drake back to the capital.

Matt Drake has been a champion of timeless electronic body music in Aotearoa for more than two decades. His style is a hypersonic melting pot of cosmic house jams and hypnotic Detroit techno grooves. Drawing inspiration from the astral arpeggios of 70s Krautrock, ragged Balearic vagabond synth pop of the 80s and proto-rave machine rhythms of the 90s.

Jen Kyle's cult following continues to grow - synonymous for her DJ sets where she journeys through everything from techno to disco, punk to funk, soul to hip hop, new wave and beyond.

Rounding out the triptych - DJ Coda can't wait to return to the CST and the opportunity to delve in and out of some different genre boxes. Hot off sets at CubaDupa and Baobab @ Newtown Festival, the courtyard is one of his favourite places to play.

Expect an Essential Selection spanned early and lates sets from all three selectors with lots of fun on and off the decks.

Make an evening of it and come for a late afternoon drink and repas (meal : ) and get into the groove when the beats start.
Early doors, early night.

venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

id: Butch Auction-level 1/60 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Butch Auction
venue: level 1/60 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

Venue is wheelchair accessible with lift access and accessible bathrooms.

id: Free Women's Self Defence Course-Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Free Women's Self Defence Course
venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

Doxing Ur Mum is a new song cycle composed by Mallory Elmo, with lyrics by poet and textile artist Anne Amber, performed by Kassandra Wang (mezzo-soprano) and Antonia Grant (violin).

long_description:
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

name: Kim Churchill LIVE at Old St Paul's, Wellington! | One-Man Band, World-Class Folk & Blues
venue: 34 Mulgrave Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
KIM CHURCHILL LIVE IN WELLINGTON!

One man. A guitar, harmonica, percussion and an extraordinary voice. A whole world of sound.

Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Kim Churchill returns to New Zealand for a very special evening of world-class live music at the beautiful Old St Paul's!

From the legendary stages of Glastonbury and the Montreal Jazz Festival to intimate venues around the world, Kim has built an international reputation for his captivating one-man-band performances, incredible guitar playing and heartfelt songwriting.

Blending folk, blues, roots and indie music, Kim creates a remarkable live experience. Intricate fingerpicking, rhythmic guitar percussion, harmonica, foot drums and soaring vocals somehow come together through just one performer.

His much-loved song Window to the Sky went platinum in Australia, and his music has reached millions of listeners around the world.

But it's on stage where Kim Churchill truly comes alive. His shows move from explosive, foot-stomping energy to beautifully intimate moments, with warmth, humour and stories from a lifetime spent travelling the world playing music.

Whether you're already a fan or discovering Kim for the first time, this is a concert not to be missed!

CONCERT DETAILS

📍 Old St Paul's, Wellington

📅 24 February 2027

🚪 Doors open 7:00pm

🎶 Concert starts 7:30pm

✨ Fully seated, intimate listening-room concert

ABOUT KIM CHURCHILL

Raised in the coastal town of Merimbula, Australia, Kim Churchill began his musical journey as a young busker before setting off around the world with a guitar, a surfboard and a remarkable talent for songwriting.

After winning the Byron Bay Bluesfest busking competition, Kim went on to perform at major international festivals, share stages with celebrated musicians and build a devoted global audience.

His distinctive one-man-band style is something that really needs to be seen to be believed. Combining technically brilliant acoustic guitar work with percussion, harmonica and a powerful, expressive voice, Kim creates a sound far bigger than one person should be capable of.

Yet beyond the extraordinary musicianship lies a gifted songwriter whose music reflects a lifelong love of travel, nature, connection and the freedom of the open road.

ABOUT THE VENUE

In the heart of Wellington, Old St Paul's is one of New Zealand's most breathtaking heritage venues, renowned for its magnificent timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and extraordinary atmosphere.

For one night, Nightingale Concerts brings its intimate listening-room experience to this iconic former church, offering audiences the chance to enjoy a remarkable Australian touring artist in one of Wellington's most beautiful and historic settings.

Expect an evening of exceptional music, heartfelt songs, extraordinary guitar playing and the kind of connection that makes live performance so special.

🎟️ TICKETS ARE ON SALE NOW!

From international festival stages to intimate concert halls around the world, Kim Churchill has captivated audiences with his extraordinary live performances.

Don't miss your chance to experience him up close in Wellington. Secure your tickets today!

name: The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"
description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous.
With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK.
Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk.
Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

id: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel-31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

long_description:
Please come along and celebrate the end of another great year with NAWIC Wellington!

We're heading to WellyPutt for a fun, relaxed evening of quirky Wellington-themed indoor, non-competitive mini golf, good company, and a chance to catch up with some familiar faces (and meet a few new ones!).

This is a relaxed evening, with plenty of opportunity to mingle, chat and enjoy the company of other women in construction. Whether you're keen to have a go at the mini golf or would rather just come along for a catch-up, we'd love to see you there.

What's included:

• A round of Wellington-themed mini golf at WellyPutt

• Plenty of nibbles and non-alcoholic drinks

• A few spot prizes throughout the evening

Tickets: $15 for NAWIC Members and $20 for Non-Members.

Arrive: anytime from 5:00 pm onwards. Come straight from work, grab a bite, have a putt and enjoy the evening.

Please note: WellyPutt is located upstairs and there is no lift access, so unfortunately the venue is not wheelchair accessible.

It's been a busy year for everyone, so this is a chance to wind down, have a laugh and celebrate another year of connections, collaboration and supporting women in construction. We hope to see you there.

NAWIC Wellington has been a long-time supporter of Wellington Women’s House, and this year we’ll again be collecting a few everyday essentials to pass on, on behalf of our generous NAWIC Wellington members.

If you’re able to bring something along, any of the following would be much appreciated.

Period products

Toothbrushes and toothpaste

Deodorant

Cutlery

Soap, shampoo or conditioner


Make sure you're following the NAWIC Wellington Humanitix page to stay in the loop and be the first to hear about upcoming events and announcements.

id: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington-71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington
venue: 71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Celebrate the richness and wonder of Christmas with Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington, as they join forces for an evening of music that spans centuries, crosses continents and brings together joyful celebration and quiet reflection.

Conducted by Ingrid Schoenfeld, who directs both, the two choirs will be accompanied by well-known organists Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting. Together, they bring a wealth of musical experience to a programme filled with colour, contrast and seasonal spirit.

At the heart of the concert is Cantata V of J.S. Bach’s Christmas Oratorio, opening with the chorus Ehre sei dir, Gott, gesungen. This part of Bach’s great Christmas work follows the journey of the Magi, exploring their search for the newborn Jesus and the image of light shining through darkness. Its combination of exuberant choral writing, storytelling and reflection offers a vivid encounter with the Christmas narrative.

Felix Mendelssohn’s Die deutsche Liturgie brings another dimension to the evening. Its Kyrie, Gloria and Sanctus move from prayerful appeal to praise and adoration, revealing the composer’s gift for expressive melody and beautifully shaped choral textures. These three movements offer moments of warmth, grandeur and stillness.

Music from Aotearoa New Zealand has a special place in this concert. Jonathan Berkahn’s Four Christmas Songs brings together Unto us a Son is given, Meditation – rorate coeli desuper, And art thou come with us to dwell? and How sweet the angels song. The sequence invites listeners to consider Christmas through proclamation, contemplation and a sense of wonder. With Berkahn also appearing as one of the evening’s organists, the concert offers a particularly personal connection between the music and its composer.

Jenny McLeod’s Vulcan and Indigo II, from her Sun Festival Carols, add further New Zealand colour.

Philip Stopford’s Lully, Lulla, Lullay provides a tender, haunting contrast. Drawing on the Coventry Carol text, it captures both the intimacy of a lullaby and the poignancy beneath the Christmas story. John Gardner’s Tomorrow shall be my dancing day brings buoyant rhythm and infectious vitality, while Mykola Leontovich’s Carol of the Bells sparkles with its familiar repeating motif and gathering excitement.

From Bach’s joyful praise to the delicacy of a lullaby, this programme offers much to discover and enjoy.

St James’ Anglican Church in Lower Hutt provides a welcoming setting, with comfortable seating and a crisp acoustic in which to savour the combined voices and accompaniment.

Make time in the busy December season for an evening of shared listening, musical discovery and festive warmth. Join Festival Singers of Wellington, Cantoris, Ingrid Schoenfeld, Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting for Bach, Bells and Christmas: a celebration of the season through the expressive power of choral music.

[Children 18 years and under enter free when accompanied by a paying adult.]

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

id: 32 Biennial New Zealand Microscopy Conference-33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: 32 Biennial New Zealand Microscopy Conference
venue: 33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
32nd New Zealand Microscopy Conference

Under the theme “Shaping the Future of Microscopy in Aotearoa New Zealand”, we warmly invite everyone involved in microscopy and microanalysis to attend our annual meeting.

This year, the conference will be held at the Pipitea Campus, Victoria University of Wellington, from 24-27 November 2026.

The conference aims to showcase advances in microscopy and microanalysis developed in New Zealand, covering a wide range of fields including biotechnology, materials science, environmental science, image analysis, artificial intelligence, data management, and homegrown technologies.

In addition, the programme will feature special interest workshops, including image analysis using QuPath, facility management, and a technology showcase.

Don’t miss out—register now!

id: AoJO November Improvisation Workshops: Advanced-Level 5/39 Webb Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: AoJO November Improvisation Workshops: Advanced
venue: Level 5/39 Webb Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Advanced

The Advanced workshop is for musicians who already have some experience with improvisation and jazz playing, or players with more advanced technique looking to dive deeper into the language of jazz.

Participants will take an in-depth look at playing jazz standards with the rhythm section, explore different styles and traditions, develop listening skills, and gain musical insights from the professional musicians leading the workshop.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

id: Lloyd Spiegel (Australia) LIVE at Old St Paul's | Wellington-34 Mulgrave Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Lloyd Spiegel (Australia) LIVE at Old St Paul's | Wellington
venue: 34 Mulgrave Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The iconic bluesman and one of Australia’s most revered live performers, Lloyd Spiegel, brings his world-famous guitar work, soulful voice, and deeply human storytelling to New Zealand in April 2027!

This is a rare chance to experience world-class artistry up close, in an intimate listening-room setting designed for focus, connection, and a true love of live music.

“A guitarist almost without peer, Spiegel deconstructs how the blues guitar is supposed to operate… makes sweet love to it, then kicks it out the back door.” — Australian Guitar Player

“Spiegel is ALL presence, authority, rhythm and drive. He epitomizes control, soul and passion with white-hot ferocity and blazing instrumental mastery.” — The Age (Melbourne)

📍 Friday 17 April 2027 @ Old St Paul's - Wellington

Seated concert

Doors 7 PM | Show 7:30 PM

Family friendly, with discounted tickets for under 18s

DON'T miss your chance to experience live music at its finest!

ABOUT LLOYD SPIEGEL

Lloyd Spiegel is a travelling bluesman at heart — a guitarist by trade and a storyteller by nature. The 14-time Australian Blues Award winner has spent a lifetime refining a signature style that honours the deep traditions of blues while pushing the music forward in his own unmistakable voice.

His performances move effortlessly between jaw-dropping guitar work, powerful vocals, humour, and deeply human moments, creating shows that feel personal, generous, and completely alive in the room.

With ten albums to his name and an international touring career spanning North America, Europe, Japan, and beyond, Lloyd is equally respected on world-class festival stages and in intimate listening rooms. At home in Australia, he is recognised as a trailblazer for blues music and has been named among the 50 greatest Australian guitarists of all time.

Whether playing to thousands or a quiet, attentive audience, Lloyd Spiegel has a rare gift for connection — making every performance feel like a shared experience, and every listener feel part of the story.

ABOUT THE VENUE

Located in the heart of Wellington, the magnificent Old St Paul’s is one of New Zealand’s most beautiful historic churches, renowned for its stunning timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and warm, intimate atmosphere.

For one special night, Nightingale Concerts transforms this breathtaking heritage landmark into a listening room, bringing audiences together to experience the extraordinary musicianship, stories, and energy of Lloyd Spiegel up close.

Expect an evening of remarkable guitar playing, powerful blues, laughter, and the kind of connection that makes live music so special.

🎟️ Tickets are ON SALE NOW! These intimate concerts have been selling out in venues around the world. With limited seating available, don't miss your chance to experience Lloyd Spiegel live in Wellington!

id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
***UPDATE: FILM WILL START AT 7:30 SHARP***

WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

-------------------------------------------------------
NOT MY SISTER - HOUSE / TECH HOUSE
Hailing from Italy and now rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister quickly burst onto Aotearoa’s dance floors and has been on a rapid rise ever since. She’s lit up festivals like Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and Arkadien and supported international acts including KC Lights.
She currently holds a radio residency on Wellington’s iconic Radio Active, where her show dives deep into house and underground sounds.
Heavily influenced by funk and disco, and driven by a love for vocals, groove and infectious pulse of 90s House, Not My Sister delivers high-energy, uplifting sets that weave together melodic basslines with soulful, tech and deep house sounds. FORTUNA - DEEP / PROGRESSIVE / MELODIC
A selector who knows exactly where the night needs to go:
Fortuna is the founder of Fortunes, a Pōneke event series devoted to the deeper end of the spectrum: deep, progressive and melodic house and techno.
Her selections run dark and sexy, all rolling momentum and slow-burn tension, the kind of set that rewards surrender. She doesn't chase the peak, she builds toward it, and the dancefloor follow.

RYAN C - TECHNO
Ryan C is a house and techno DJ based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), NZ.
He spent his formative years travelling solo around the desolate Southern African coast, the stars his blanket and the ocean his teacher.
After being missing for 14 years, he was ‘liberated’ by the Red Cross in Northern Africa ‘working’ on an Ethiopian pirate ship in the Gulf of Aden.
He was in desperate need of revitalisation, so was moved to their base deep in the Amazon basin, in Peru, near the border of Brazil, where he was healed by Amazonian Shamans using an ancient technique.
The Amazonian tribe then guided him by canoe through the Amazon river to the coast of Brazil where he found a group of underground tribal techno-heads living on an island and learnt the ways of techno. After finding out about an illustrious island in the South-Pacific where the earth moves and sky is painted with lava from deep inside the earth, he made his way to Aotearoa where he continues his search inwards, through music.
You'll also find me hosting the Midnight Marauders radio show on Radio Active Friday nights 11-1am!

https://www.instagram.com/ryanc.nz/

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

long_description:
Christmas Fantasia

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul, 2 Hill Street, Thorndon


General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

School-aged children free


Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant
