id: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman-Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

NYMPHO welcomes Chippy Nonstop to Pōneke in collaboration with her own party series, PEP RALLY, for a cross-continental meeting on the dancefloor. One for the history books.

Chippy Nonstop is a versatile DJ, rapper, and producer whose high-energy sets seamlessly blend global club, rap, and bass-driven sounds. She thrives across contexts from queer-focused underground nights to fashion events and more commercial stages bringing her unique energy to every floor. Key shows include Berghain, Live From Earth, DGTL, Ultra, the Mugler Fashion Show and has shared lineups with VTSS, LSDXOXO, Honey Dijon and many more. Chippy also runs her own party series and upcoming label Pep Rally, centering FLINTA, BIPOC, and queer representation*.

NYMPHO is a dance-focused queer club night with visual and performance art styles woven into high energy DJ sets. We strive to create a safe, inclusive and transcendent club experience which celebrates gender euphoria, body positivity and sexual liberation. Our kaupapa of lifting up marginalised communities extends from our audience and lineups to our musical philosophies - with genre-diverse sets centred around QBIPOC rooted genres such as techno, house and emergent queer sounds. As well as spotlighting the best of Aotearoa’s diverse queer talent, NYMPHO has brought international icons to our long white cloud, including Isabella Lovestory, horsegiirL, Doss, TAAHLIAH, Ninajirachi, Umru, MGNA Crrrta, Kevin Aviance, MikeQ, Pxssy Palace, Jasmine Infiniti, Estoc, Clearcast and DJ G2G.

Ki ngā iwi Mana Whenua ō Te Whanganui-a-Tara, tēnei te tuku mihi ki ā koutou katoa. We acknowledge Te Āti Awa, Ngāti Mutunga, Ngāti Tama, Ngāti Ruanui, Taranaki Whānui, Ngāti Toa Rangatira as Mana Whenua of Wellington/Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

id: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)-311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)
venue: 311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Living with ADHD can be tiring. Constantly trying harder.

Wondering why things that seem simple for other people can feel so difficult.

Liminal is a workshop designed to help make sense of that experience — and to help you discover practical ways forward.

This isn’t about fixing yourself. It’s about working with how you’re wired.

You’ll leave with:

a clearer understanding of why your ADHD works the way it does

practical strategies you can begin using immediately

hope that life can become easier

Rather than leaving with another list of things you "should" do, you'll leave with one or two small experiments that fit your own life.

What we'll explore

ADHD: why it works the way it does, and why life can feel so much harder than it should.

Emotional regulation: sometimes one of the most overlooked parts of ADHD.

Executive functioning: why starting, planning, remembering, and following through can be so difficult.

Dopamine: motivation, energy, and why "just try harder" rarely works.

Tiny Habits®: a simple, practical way to begin making lasting changes.

Liminal offers education and practical support; it doesn’t replace professional care, provide diagnosis or offer advice about medication.

Who is this for?

This workshop is best suited to adults (16+) who already have some understanding of ADHD — whether diagnosed, self-identified, exploring or supporting someone in your whanau.

However, anyone is welcome.

Come as you are.
You don't need to have everything sorted.
Just bring your curiosity.

Details at a glance

Date: Saturday 28th November 2026

Venue: St Hilda's Church, 11 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington

Time:

10.00am - Registration, coffee, snacks

10.15am - Workshop begins

12.30ish. Light lunch (included)

2.30pm - Finish

What’s included

Coffee and snacks, light lunch

Workbook materials (new and revamped; including an experiment guide)

A chance to reflect, connect, and further develop your own individual plan

Cost

Individual: $70

Couple: $110

Multiple: Two from one family/whanau: $110

For unwaged tickets ($40) or larger family groups please contact Derek on 021 511 303. You can get an access code to for a group discount.

Some sponsored (free) places are available.

Register by

Please register by the Thursday prior (26th November).

If are signing up . . .

If you have any questions, any information it may be helpful for me to know or requests, please call,

Presenter: Derek Chirnside

Over the past twenty years I've listened to many of adults describe what ADHD feels like from the inside. Again and again I hear similar themes: feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, shamed, huge creativity, humour, resilience, and the longing to simply make life work a little better. Also, timeblindness and hyperfocus!

This workshop grew out of those conversations.

I'm based in Christchurch. I've worked as a classroom teacher, teacher educator (including training teachers to support students with ADHD), university chaplain, and business owner. I'm a long-time ADHD educator with a particular focus on practical, sustainable strategies that help adults live well with ADHD. More information on website

Learningworkshops.nz

Questions?

long_description:
Let’s talk about grief.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a series of free community conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O’Connor for an honest, informal conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the tidy timelines, clichés and expectations we’re often given.

There is no right kind of grief, and no right way to show up.

You might be grieving someone you love. You might be supporting someone who is. You might work alongside grief in your community or simply want us to get better at talking about something that touches all of us.

You are welcome to come and listen. You don’t have to share your story, speak, or have the right words.

Come as you are.

long_description:
EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

name: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Undercurrent, Wellington, NZ
venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Special guest: Joe Cole

long_description:
"Every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings" — Zuzu, It’s a Wonderful Life

Dementia Wellington invites you to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Frank Capra's inspiring Christmas classic It’s a Wonderful Life with your whānau and friends in the lavish Embassy Theatre.

Proceeds from this event will help Dementia Wellington provide community-based specialised support services for those experiencing dementia across the wider Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington area.

A fundraising afternoon tea will be served from 2:30pm. Seasonal, Tiered Cake Stands containing goodies and treats can be purchased to take into the Movie for sharing and enjoying. Your stand will be disassembled, wrapped and bagged for you to take home.

After the movie, a symbol of hope made by one of our Dementia Friends – a "Zuzu's Rose Petal" – will be available for you to take home as well. You are welcome to make a petal yourself to leave for someone else.

"My thanks go to you, young and old, for supporting Dementia Wellington with our work. Your generosity, as always, makes such a difference. Our team looks forward to seeing you on 13 December at this celebrated Christmas holiday tradition. My very best wishes."

Stephanie Clare, Chief Executive, Dementia Wellington

We look forward to enjoying this very special film with you and your loved ones this December in support of Dementia Wellington and encourage you to spread the word!

Tickets can also be acquired on the day.


If you would like to check out a little more about the man spearheading the whole event, check out this interview!

Our friends Anji and James Foster from Lowe&Co have made an amazing promotional.

venue: Colombo St & Rintoul St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
embroidery with beads workshop: Slow Down. Make something.

Join me for a cozy, beginner-friendly embroidery workshop designed for adults who want to learn something new and enjoy a creative evening together.

In this 2hour session, I’ll guide you through the basic stitches you need to get started with hand embroidery and help you start your own project on your item of clothing.

We’ll begin by practicing on small fabric squares so you can build confidence and get comfortable with your needle and thread, practice how to attach beads before starting a project onto a piece of clothing you’ve brought along or a piece of fabric from my stash — turning it into something beautifully personal and unique.

This workshop is all about slowing down, crafting together, and enjoying the process in a relaxed, welcoming space.

All materials are provided, and you’ll head home with:

A piece of practice fabric + a blank square for your next project

An embroidery hoop, needle, some thread and the fabric you need to finish your project



Soft drinks (hot and cold) and snacks will also be available to keep our creative energy flowing.

No experience is needed — just bring an item of clothing you’d love to transform (or a bag, a pouch, anything you can stitch on) and a willingness to try something new. I can’t wait to stitch with you 🤍

Please note, the workshop will be cancelled if less than 3 participants are signed up 7 days prior to the date.

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

name: Gong Bath at Vogelmorn Hall
venue: 13 Vennell Street, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
$25

Limited door sales for $30

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

This November, we’re bringing a taste of Martinborough to the Thistle for a special evening with Palliser, as part of Taste of Wairarapa.

For one night, our kitchen and Palliser have come together on a four-course menu with matched wines, with each dish crafted around what’s being poured alongside it.

Joining us at the table is Palliser winemaker Guy McMaster, who’ll take us through the wines as the evening unfolds - from the first glass through to the final course.

It’s a chance to settle in for four courses, discover some brilliant Wairarapa wines, and hear a little more about what goes into each bottle from the person behind them.

Event Details

The Thistle Inn

Wednesday 18 November

6:00pm

Four-course menu with matched Palliser wines

Tickets: $145 per person

Seats are limited.

JOURNEY: THE BREAKTHROUGH (⭐Most Popular)

Activating, Energising, Releasing

Prepare for the unexplainable: This journey is an all-rounded architecture of sound, audio and visualisation. 💎 Access to Coaching Frameworks

💎 The State Change Toolkit

💎 Exclusive Bonus Offer to Attendees

Arrival Time: 
Please arrive 15 minutes before the advertised start time to say hello and get settled in.

Food Prep Tip:

Although this event is not recommended for some people, the experience can be tailored for individual needs and made safe for all. Please refer to FAQs for more info.

Media notice: During the event we will be capturing photo and video content as a part of our commitment to sharing the power of 9D Breathwork with the world online. You acknowledge that by attending this event, you give your consent to allow full room photo and video to be recorded, and for it to be published and/or used by Beyond Ordinary on our website, in printed materials, and on social media platforms, and waive copyrights and rights to compensation for this.

Your Facilitators

Olivia Hoebers
Certified 9D Breathwork™ Facilitator
Teacher & Trauma-Informed Coach

As a registered primary school teacher, homebased care provider, trauma-informed coach trained through the Elementum Coaching Institute, 9D Breathwork facilitator, and mother, I bring a unique blend of professional expertise and lived experience to supporting individuals, couples, families, and school communities.

From navigating pregnancy, birth and postpartum as a solo mother to building a life and business with my partner, my own experiences have shaped how I work with others. Drawing on a decade of learning and practice across education, breathwork, NLP, Parts Therapy and somatic release, I offer an approach that is integrative, intuitive and grounded in both knowledge and experience. I know this work, and I love what I do.

https://www.instagram.com/witholiviajane/

Jay Kahu
Certified Rebirth™ Breathwork Practitioner
Transformation & Trauma-Informed Coach

Father of 4, and founder of Self-Made: Men’s Group, I work with clients 1:1, couples, groups, corporate and facilitate events across New Zealand. I use breathwork & coaching as my tools to help people heal, release, and reconnect with themselves on a deeper level. This is my passion and my purpose is to serve those willing to go the extra mile to live an extraordinary life!

Alongside my partner, Olivia, I co-create powerful community-based events that support embodiment, awareness, and transformation. I bring real-life experience, intuitive leadership, and heart-led facilitation to every room I step into.

https://www.instagram.com/iamjaykahu/

We don't just facilitate, we Coach.

We work with people around:

→ Mapping the mind: understanding the patterns, beliefs and stories running beneath the surface.

→ Navigating emotions: learning to feel, process and move through what comes up.

→ Shifting identity: letting go of outdated versions of yourself and creating space for who you're becoming.

→ Building a relationship with self: developing greater awareness, trust and connection with yourself and a higher purpose.


OUR GUARANTEE

We guarantee that this back-to-back event will impact your life moving forward. 9D Breathwork isn't just a cognitive upgrade. It goes deeper beneath the surface of the analytical mind. 9D audio impacts the mind while somatic body-based breathwork aligns the connection between the two.


GUARANTED TO SHIFT MORE THAT JUST AWARENESS ALONE.


The waters still murky and vision unclear?

After going through every process with the willingness to show up fully, if you are still unsure of what to do next, you will receive a free 20 minute coaching call with Jay to clear things up. This guarantee is valid up to 2 weeks post-event.


If nothing shifts* for you by the end of this event, knowing that you have participated at your highest level of integrity toward your own commitment through this process; You may receive a 100% money back guarantee.

Mental

Physical

Emotional

Energetic

name: The Velvet Glove Plays the Songs of The Velvet Underground
venue: 52 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The Velvet Glove returns following last January’s breakout show to revisit the heart of the Velvet Underground’s gritty urban realism, bridging the Velvet’s bright jangly chaos and Lou Reed’s lyric beauty.

 

The Glove reunites three musicians from early 70s Dunedin Band Cripple - bass player John Dodd (Midge Marsden, The Chaps, Skin and Bone), sax player Chris Nichol (The Dunstan Rangers, The Zimmermans) and Lindsay Gregory (The Dunstan Rangers, Heaven Bent Choir) on keyboards. They’re joined by drummer Sean Barker (Wooden Box Band, The Zimmermans) and guitarist Bill Nichol (Baby, Pegasus) for another walk on the wild side.

name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

name: "It's A Wonderful Life" 80th Anniversary Screening
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
"Every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings" — Zuzu, It’s a Wonderful Life

Dementia Wellington invites you to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Frank Capra's inspiring Christmas classic It’s a Wonderful Life with your whānau and friends in the lavish Embassy Theatre.

Proceeds from this event will help Dementia Wellington provide community-based specialised support services for those experiencing dementia across the wider Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington area.

A fundraising afternoon tea will be served from 2:30pm. Seasonal, Tiered Cake Stands containing goodies and treats can be purchased to take into the Movie for sharing and enjoying. Your stand will be disassembled, wrapped and bagged for you to take home.

After the movie, a symbol of hope made by one of our Dementia Friends – a "Zuzu's Rose Petal" – will be available for you to take home as well. You are welcome to make a petal yourself to leave for someone else.

"My thanks go to you, young and old, for supporting Dementia Wellington with our work. Your generosity, as always, makes such a difference. Our team looks forward to seeing you on 13 December at this celebrated Christmas holiday tradition. My very best wishes."

Stephanie Clare, Chief Executive, Dementia Wellington

We look forward to enjoying this very special film with you and your loved ones this December in support of Dementia Wellington and encourage you to spread the word!

Tickets can also be acquired on the day.


If you would like to check out a little more about the man spearheading the whole event, check out this interview!

Our friends Anji and James Foster from Lowe&Co have made an amazing promotional.

long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!

long_description:
Indie alt-rockers 'Homing" farewell 2026 with an intimate, exclusive, and first-class evening of live music.

Homing invite you to join them at Vogelmorn Bowling Club on Friday, December 11th for their final show of 2026. After a year of successful performances across the Wellington region and beyond, Homing make their debut headlining show at Vogelmorn Upstairs, presenting an intricate, focused, and engaging collection of authentically crafted songs, backed by alt-country and indie-rock influence.

To open the evening, Sebastian Bell (Felix Bird, Jack Bromwich), re-emerges into the alt/indie scene with his live band to showcase some of his latest and solo works. To complete the lineup, Elly Mae comes forth with a deeply emotional and tastefully melancholic library of alt-indie grooves. With each live appearance sculpted to lyrical, musical. and compositional perfection, Elly Mae and her live band consistently reach into Wellington audiences with delicate and rhythmic trance.

Secure tickets now to be a part of this very special evening of exceptional talent at Vogelmorn Upstairs.

id: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Petone Depot, Petone, NZ-8/193 Jackson Street, Petone, Lower Hutt 5012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Petone Depot, Petone, NZ
venue: 8/193 Jackson Street, Petone, Lower Hutt 5012, New Zealand
long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

id: NYMPHO X PEP RALLY (PŌNEKE WELLINGTON)-38 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: NYMPHO X PEP RALLY (PŌNEKE WELLINGTON)
venue: 38 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
NYMPHO welcomes Chippy Nonstop to Pōneke in collaboration with her own party series, PEP RALLY, for a cross-continental meeting on the dancefloor. One for the history books.

Chippy Nonstop is a versatile DJ, rapper, and producer whose high-energy sets seamlessly blend global club, rap, and bass-driven sounds. She thrives across contexts from queer-focused underground nights to fashion events and more commercial stages bringing her unique energy to every floor. Key shows include Berghain, Live From Earth, DGTL, Ultra, the Mugler Fashion Show and has shared lineups with VTSS, LSDXOXO, Honey Dijon and many more. Chippy also runs her own party series and upcoming label Pep Rally, centering FLINTA, BIPOC, and queer representation*.

LINEUP:

CHIPPY NONSTOP (CAN)

BABETECH

CURRENT BIAS

WELMIE

ODEIOUS

DOOM100001B2B75ARROWHEADS

MC MAN(K)ILA

NYMPHO is a dance-focused queer club night with visual and performance art styles woven into high energy DJ sets. We strive to create a safe, inclusive and transcendent club experience which celebrates gender euphoria, body positivity and sexual liberation. Our kaupapa of lifting up marginalised communities extends from our audience and lineups to our musical philosophies - with genre-diverse sets centred around QBIPOC rooted genres such as techno, house and emergent queer sounds. As well as spotlighting the best of Aotearoa’s diverse queer talent, NYMPHO has brought international icons to our long white cloud, including Isabella Lovestory, horsegiirL, Doss, TAAHLIAH, Ninajirachi, Umru, MGNA Crrrta, Kevin Aviance, MikeQ, Pxssy Palace, Jasmine Infiniti, Estoc, Clearcast and DJ G2G.

Ki ngā iwi Mana Whenua ō Te Whanganui-a-Tara, tēnei te tuku mihi ki ā koutou katoa. We acknowledge Te Āti Awa, Ngāti Mutunga, Ngāti Tama, Ngāti Ruanui, Taranaki Whānui, Ngāti Toa Rangatira as Mana Whenua of Wellington/Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

May the flames of your peoples never extinguish, but only to burn brighter. Thank you for your enduring presence! Mauri Ora!! 🖤🤍❤️

Concession tickets are available for low wage, unemployed or financially insecure nymphs. If you can't afford a ticket you can get in touch with us via Instagram. No nymphs left behind!

EPILEPSY WARNING: Strobe lighting and other intense lighting effects will be used during this show. It will not be safe for those with epilepsy and other conditions with sensitivity to light.

id: Sunday Jazz ft. Fritz Wollner Trio-118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Sunday Jazz ft. Fritz Wollner Trio
venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
This Sunday presents Fritz Wollner Trio!

For this one Fritz Wollner (Piano) is teaming up with "regular around towners" Daniel Yeabsley on Bass and John Rae on drums to play a new selection of Fritz's favourite Jazz Standards. Fritz, who has been living in New Zealand for 40 years raising a family and teaching at Wellington High School, is coming back to performing music after a long break. He has played in various groups around Wellington in the last 30 years before the job of Head of Music at WHS took too much time and energy. In retirement he has spent an increasing amount of time getting back into music and is now ready to share his passion with an audience again. 

After the first two "Undercurrent Sunday Sessions" earlier this year people commented on the Trios melodic and spacious approach to the timeless classics. So this one sees them back with a new set of favourites.

Sunday Nov 15

Doors 3pm

Music 3:30pm

$15 ($25 support the artist)

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆
